Spiky shield and baneful bunker do block status moves. They are the only individual protecting move variants with additional effects upon making contact that don't just block attacking moves. Thousand arrows can hit flying type Pokémon, but it will only ever be for neutral damage. A flying steel type Pokémon and a flying bug type Pokémon will both take neutral damage from thousand arrows. This is the same for a flying type holding an iron ball with regular ground moves. They will always take neutral damage. However, a flying type in gravity can be hit for super effective or resisted damage by regular ground moves depending on its secondary type. Proto synthesis and cork drive boost the user's highest stat by 30%, 50% for speed, but Orichalcum Pulse always boosts attack by 33% and Hadron Engine always boosts special attack by 33%. Moonblast is not a ball and bomb move, so it is not blocked by bullet proof. It just has a similar animation to many ball and bomb moves. The flame orb and toxic orb will only activate if whatever action that was taken costed a turn. Using your turn to switch into an orb holder will cause them to activate at the end of the turn. Using a pivoting move and switching into them will cause them to activate. If one Pokémon faints and then you switch into an orb holder, it will not activate at the end of the turn. This all applies to Moody as well, but it does not apply to speed boost. Speed boost will never activate on a Pokémon switching in. Wide guard and quick guard can be used multiple times in a row without increasing their chance of failing. However, if you use protect or any other individual protecting move variant on the following turn, they will be treated as if protect was used successfully on all of those turns. So, they will have a one in three, one in nine, or one in whatever chance of being used successfully depending on how many times wide guard or quick guard were used. A perfectly accurate move such as aerial ace will miss a Pokémon on a semi-invulnerable turn. However, a move used by or against a no guard user will hit a Pokémon on a semi-invulnerable turn, and same with lock on and mind reader, and a poison type using toxic. As of Champions, fake out doesn't fail if used after the first turn a Pokémon is sent out. It straight up cannot be selected. This is also now the case for first impression, which by the way got buffed to 100 power in Champions. Soak and magic powder change the target Pokémon's type to pure water and pure psychic respectively. Forest's curse and trick or treat add the grass and ghost types respectively to the target Pokémon's existing type. These two cannot stack with each other, and their effect goes away upon terastallization. Blunder policy will not activate when missing an Ogle move, when missing any hit after the first hit of triple kick, triple axle, or population bomb, or when missing a target due to them being in a semi-invulnerable turn. Form-changing items such as mega stones and ogre pond's masks cannot be knocked off, and knock off will not receive the 1.5 times power boost. A Pokémon with sticky hold will also not have their item knocked off, but knock off will receive the 1.5 times power boost. Bad poison's turn counter will still go up if the inflicted Pokémon has magic guard or poison heal. If they've been out for five turns and get their ability changed or nullified, they will take 5/16 max HP worth of bad poison damage on that turn. Burn works by multiplying the inflicted Pokémon's damage by 0.5 on physical moves, which is why it makes body press and foul play weaker. It is not a base power modifier like Showdown suggests, although this distinction really isn't super impactful in the grand scheme of damage calculations. Spread moves, moves that hit multiple Pokémon in a double or triple battle, will have their damage cut by 25% or a 0.75 times multiplier as long as at least two Pokémon are targeted. Targeting more than two Pokémon will not change the multiplier. Hitting into an immunity, a protect, or missing a target will also not change the multiplier. Z-Moves are completely unaffected by moves that restrict the use of other moves. A Z status move can still be used through taunt. A Z attacking move can still be used if the Pokémon was Encore'd into another move. A Pokémon must survive the attack for the Red Card item to switch out the attacker. If an attacking move knocks out a Pokémon holding the Red Card, the item will not activate. Tera has a hidden mechanic of increasing the power of moves of the Tera type with a base power below 60 up to 60 when Terastallized. This does not apply to multi strike moves or priority moves, and it also happens after all other base power modifiers, meaning that it typically won't be able to stack with them. The specifics of it are quite confusing, so check out this Pink Across video for a more in-depth explanation. The Serene Grace ability in the rainbow from Water and Fire Pledge do stack for all moves' secondary effects except flinching. Despite not directly being a secondary effect of a move, the flinch chance added to moves by the King's Rock will have its chance doubled by either Serene Grace or the rainbow, but again, not both. King's Rock and Stench do not add an additional flinch chance to moves that already have a chance to flinch, and they also do not stack with each other. On multi-strike moves, the King's Rock or Stench will add a flinch chance to each individual hit. To calculate the chance of at least one hit flinching, you do 1 minus the chance to not flinch to the power of how many times hit. Starting in Gen 3, critical hits ignore the user's negative attack and special attack stat changes, and the target's positive defense and special defense stat changes, as well as reflect, light screen, and Aurora Veil. If the user has positive stat changes, or the target has negative stat changes, that is still factored in. Basically, from their most up-to-date effect, critical hits are always beneficial and can only ever make you deal more damage. Burn and non-stat change, non-screen defense boosts, such as the Assault Vest, will still be factored in, though. One-hit knockout moves do not use the traditional accuracy formula, but rather this formula, and they are also not affected by any effect that modifies accuracy. They can, however, be made to have perfect accuracy by No Guard, Mind Reader, and Lock-On. Body Press is only different from regular attacking moves in that it uses the user's effective defense stat and defense boosts instead of effective attack stat and attack boosts. All other modifiers are what they are normally for physical attacks. Body Press's damage is reduced from burn, unaffected by the user's reflect, Fur Coat, or held Eviolite, and increased by Choice Band, Huge Power, and Sword of Ruin. Foul Play is only different from regular attacking moves in that it uses the target's effective attack stat and attack boosts instead of the user's effective attack stat and attack boosts. Like Body Press, all other modifiers are what they are normally. Foul Play's damage is reduced from the user's burn and increased by the user's stab, user's damage-increasing abilities like huge power, and user's damage-increasing items like the choice band. Status moves do not maintain type effectiveness except for one, Thunder Wave. Ghost type Pokémon can be hit by Roar, Flying type Pokémon can be hit by Sand Attack, and so on. Fire types are immune to Will-O-Wisp because of Fire's secondary immunity to burn. Electric types are immune to Thunder Wave because of Electric's secondary immunity to paralysis. Poison and Steel types are immune to Toxic because of Poison and Steel's secondary immunity to poison. Steel's primary immunity to Poison type damaging moves has nothing to do with its immunity to Poison type status moves that inflict the poison status condition. If a Steel type holds the Ring Target, it will still be immune to Toxic. If a Ground type holds the Ring Target, it will be affected by Thunder Wave since the reason that it's immune normally is because Thunder Wave maintains type effectiveness, not because Ground types are immune to paralysis. They are not. Ghost type Pokémon are immune to all forms of trapping, not just the trapping effect from Shadow Tag. A Ghost Steel type is still immune to the trapping effect of Magnet Pull. When a Pokémon with Guts is burned, it doesn't half its attack and then increase its attack. Guts Pokémon ignore the damage reduction on physical moves from burn entirely and only get their attack increased. Same goes for paralysis and quick feet. It doesn't half the user's speed and then increase speed. It only increases speed. They will both suffer the other consequences of burn and paralysis, though, taking chip damage every turn and having a chance to be fully paralyzed. Upper Hand has plus three priority, which is the same as fake out. So, an Upper Hand user has to be faster than the opposing fake out user for it to work. Upper Hand also only works on priority attacking moves. So, it fails completely if the target uses a priority status move. Some special moves do make contact. Petal Dance, Trump Card, Ring Out, Grass Knot, Draining Kiss, Infestation, and Electro Drift all make contact. The 20% boost from Iron Fist and the 10% boost from Punching Glove do indeed stack for a 32% or 1.32 times boost. Bulbapedia incorrectly stated that they did not in March of 2023, but corrected it in June. Clear Body, White Smoke, Full Metal Body, Mist, the Clear Amulet, Flower Veil, or any other effect that prevents stat drops does not prevent self-inflicted stat drops like the ones from Superpower, Close Combat, and Overheat. They also do not prevent stat changes from being reset from Haze or Clear Smog. Defiant and Competitive will only activate when an opposing Pokémon lowers your stats. Lowering your allies' stats in a double battle with something like Parting Shot will not activate Defiant or Competitive. Having positive stat changes reset from Haze or Clear Smog will also not activate Defiant or Competitive. Sand Rush, Sand Veil, and Sand Force cause the user to not take damage from sandstorm if they aren't already immune from their typing in addition to their other effects. And Snow Cloak and Ice Body are the same for hail. However, Slush Rush does not prevent the user from taking hail damage if they aren't already immune. This is almost never relevant though because all Slush Rush users are Ice type and hail was changed to snow in Gen 9, which doesn't deal any chip damage. Dragon Claw, X-Scissor, Dire Claw, Stone Axe, and Ceaseless Edge do not have high critical hit ratios in the main games, only in Legends: Arceus. Regigigas does not have an ability in Legends: Arceus because the game does not have abilities at all. Slow Start was instead reworked into a Regigigas exclusive status condition that acts like an ability. Each individual hit of a multi-strike move increases the power of Rage Fist. Using a four-hit Beat Up on Annihilape charges Rage Fist to 250 power and it has a cap of 350 after six total hits. Last Respects is a similar move in that it starts out at 50 power and increases by an additional 50 every time an ally has fainted, but it has a much higher cap at 5,050 after 100 allies faint. This is only possible because of the move Revival Blessing, where you faint and revive 100 times. From Black and White to Scarlet and Violet, Rapid Spin will not clear hazards and Knock Off will not remove the target's item if the user faints from Rocky Helmet, Rough Skin, or Iron Barbs. This was changed in Champions so that even if the user faints, those secondary effects will still occur. STAB is a 50% or 1.5 times damage modifier on moves that are the same type as one of the user's types. Adaptability changes the STAB modifier from 1.5 to two. Terastallizing into one of your original types also changes the STAB modifier from 1.5 to two. Terastallizing a Pokémon with Adaptability makes it so that the Tera type, and only the Tera type, will have a two-times power boost, 2.25 if the Tera type was one of the user's original types. A type-less Pokémon using a type-less move will not receive typeless stab. Typeless Pokemon cannot receive stab on any attack in any way. Wonder Guard cannot be skill swapped. It also cannot be copied by receiver or power of alchemy, and wandering spirit will fail with Wonder Guard. It can, however, be copied by trace or passed by Entrainment, which are the only ways for Wonder Guard to legitimately be given to a Pokemon other than Shedinja. Attack, defense, special attack, special defense, and speed stat modifiers work slightly different from evasiveness and accuracy. For attack through speed, start out at 2/2. +1 stage increases the numerator by 1, and -1 stage increases the denominator by 1. Accuracy starts out at 3/3, with +1 stage increasing the numerator by 1, and -1 stage increasing the denominator by 1. Evasiveness also starts out at 3/3, but the modifier is flipped, so +1 stage increases the denominator by 1, and -1 stage increases the numerator by 1. Accuracy and evasiveness stat changes don't stack multiplicatively. Using a move with -1 accuracy against a target with +1 evasiveness will not have an accuracy of 56.25% or 3/4 squared, but rather 60% or 3/5. You take the combined total of stat stage changes that decrease accuracy, and add that to the denominator of the multiplier, which again starts out at 3/3. This has a hard cap at -6, a 3/9 multiplier, which is why in setups to make the lowest possible accuracy, it's useless to have an opponent with +6 evasiveness if you already have a Pokemon with -6 accuracy. Sheer Force will only cancel out Life Orb damage if the move used is boosted by Sheer Force. Using a move without a removable secondary effect will still cause you to take LifeOrb damage. Misty Terrain does not boost fairy moves except for Misty Explosion. Grassy, Electric, and Psychic Terrain only boost Grass, Electric, and Psychic moves by 30% if the user is grounded. A priority move fails if the target is on Psychic Terrain. Expanding Force becomes spread if the user is on Psychic Terrain. Rising Voltage deals double damage if the target is on Electric Terrain. Psycho Shock, Psycho Strike, and Secret Sword deal physical damage, but they are still considered special moves. They have their damage reduced by Light Screen, not Reflect, and activate Mirror Coat, not Counter. However, both Fur Coat and Ice Scales reduce the damage from these moves because Fur Coat works by doubling defense, and Ice Scales works by halving the damage dealt by special moves. A slight distinction that does matter here. Type immune abilities will grant an immunity to status moves of that type, but only if that ability also grants a damage boost, HP restoration, or stat increase. A Pokémon with Earth Eater is immune to Sand Attack, since Earth Eater restores HP, but a Pokémon with Levitate is not immune to Sand Attack, since Levitate doesn't grant a boost of any kind. Type immune abilities with additional effects will only activate once on multi-strike moves. Using Surging Strikes on a Water Absorb mon will only heal it once. Using Bullet Seed on a Sap Sipper mon will only raise attack by one stage. Flying Press is not a flying type move, but rather a fighting type move with the unique property of dealing fighting and flying type damage simultaneously. Hawlucha does not receive double stab on it, and a mono flying type would not receive any stab on it. It has its damage reduced by the Chople Berry, never the Cobba Berry. Sandstorm is a field condition that lasts five turns and deals chip damage every turn, but on the fifth turn, it ends before the chip damage goes off, so it will only chip four times. Grassy Terrain is another five-turn field condition that heals every turn, but on the fifth turn, it ends after the healing, so Pokémon will be healed five times. Hitting into a protect does not count as a move failing to double the power of stomping tantrum or temper flare. Neither does missing one opponent on a spread move. You would have to miss both opponents for the power to be doubled. Psychic Terrain will not block priority moves that target an ally in a double battle, regardless of being grounded or not. Same goes for dark types not blocking prankster-boosted moves if it comes from an ally. Pressure does not double the use of a move's PP. It makes you use one more than normal if that move targets a Pokémon with pressure. If two opposing Pokémon have pressure in a double battle, you will use one PP on most self-targeting moves, two PP on a single-target move that targets one of the pressure mons, and three PP on a spread move. Multiple eject buttons and multiple eject packs cannot activate from one move. Only the one that has its activation condition met first will go off, with a tie going to the holder with the highest speed. Showdown does this incorrectly because they will both activate, but will not on cartridge. A red card and one of these ejecting items can both activate from one move, and this is how it works on cart as of Scarlet and Violet. Huge power, pure power, and fur coat do not affect base stats, but rather effective stats, which is the number that you see on the stat summary screen. Doubling the base stat is not the same as doubling the raw stat. If you and your opponent both only have one Pokémon left and you knock out their Pokémon with a recoil move that also knocks you out, you win. There are certain moves where you will lose, such as if you use explosion, but check out this video from Matt Bud for a more in-depth look. All of them will count as whiting out in a trainer or wild battle in a playthrough. A Pokémon does not have to be grounded for the terrain seeds to activate. Flying types and levitators can use the terrain seeds just fine. The going first or last in your priority bracket effects do not change dynamically. This includes the items lagging tail, quick claw, and custap berry, and the abilities stall, mycelium might, and quick draw. All of these effects are determined at the start of the turn and cannot be changed by anything that happens throughout the turn, unlike the speed stat, which starting in gen 8 does update dynamically between moves used within a turn. Priority effects can change in the middle of a turn. If a Weezing is neutralizing prankster in a double battle, switching it out will cause prankster to activate on that turn, and switching it in will cause prankster to not activate on that turn. Using a rampaging move, such as outrage or raging fury, only uses up PP the first time the move is selected. Being on a rampage also does not count as using the same move twice in a row for torment because you don't have the choice of selecting that move once you're on the rampage. Belly drum takes away half max HP, but it rounds down, so you need to have even HP for it to activate the citrus berry from full health, since the citrus berry activates at 50% or less HP. However, Shed Tail rounds up, so even or odd HP will cause the Sitrus Berry to activate when used from full health. The normal type move changing abilities, aka the eight and eyes abilities, do not grant power boost to moves that are already the type that the ability changes to. So, a Sylveon will not receive any power boost on Moon Blast from Pixilate. However, Normalize does. So, a Delcatty using Double-Edge will receive a power boost from Normalize. A Terastallized Pokémon cannot have its type removed or changed by any means. So, moves and abilities like Roost, Soak, Forest's Curse, Protean, and Double Shock will not have any type changing or removing effect. Roost will still heal, but the Pokémon will stay flying type. Dry Skin increases the damage taken from fire type moves by 1.25 times, while Fluffy increases the damage taken from fire type moves by two times. Fluffy also halves the damage taken from contact moves, so a fire type move that makes contact will deal normal damage. Parental Bond does not affect moves that already hit multiple times. It also does not affect spread moves, although it does in singles or if there's only one target left in doubles, like if all other Pokémon are knocked out. Aurora Veil only needs snow to be up when the move is set. So, if snow runs out or is overridden while Aurora Veil is up, it will stay up and will still be in effect for as many turns as it has left, regardless of the current weather. Aurora Veil does not stack with Light Screen or Reflect. I think there may have been a time where Showdown did this incorrectly, but I couldn't find anything for sure. They also all have different modifiers in singles compared to doubles. In singles, they reduce damage by half, making it about the equivalent of having plus two defense or special defense. In doubles, they reduce damage by 33% regardless of how many Pokémon are actually on the battlefield, about the equivalent of having plus one defense or special defense. Punching Glove outright prevents punching moves from making contact, so if an ability requires contact to be made for it to activate, such as Unseen Fist, that requirement will not be met. Protective Pads just protects the holder from any adverse effects of contact, so contact will still be made and the requirement for those contact-dependent abilities will be met. Emergency Exit, Berserk, and Anger Shell will not activate if the user's HP gets to half or below from a substitute or other self-damage dealing status move. It must be from opponent-inflicted or ally-inflicted direct damage, although Emergency Exit can activate from recoil damage. None of them will activate multiple times from one move, like when hit by a multi-strike move while holding a Sitrus Berry. It will only activate after all hits. If Knock Off is used on a dark-weak Pokémon holding the Colbur Berry, the Colbur Berry will still be in effect and Knock Off will still be 1.5 times power boosted. In most cases, if an item has an effect dependent upon getting hit and hitting that Pokémon with Knock Off satisfies that condition, the item will activate and then it will be removed if it was not already consumed. The exceptions I was able to find were the Eject Button and Kee Berry, which will be removed before having a chance to activate. And finally, a bonus misconception that's not Pokémon related, five is not the middle on a scale of one to 10. If you define middle as median, 5.5 is the middle because one through 10 has an even number of values and there is no perfect middle when the sample size is even. The middle would be the average between the two middle numbers. If you define middle as mean, 5.5 would still be the middle. On a scale of zero to 10, five would be the middle because now there's an odd number of values, so there is a perfect median and five would also be the mean. And those are 69 Pokémon mechanic misconceptions.
